title: Fenwick Systems - Governance-Heavy Onboarding / Sprint Zero Intake

SE discussed high-level rollout plan, benchmarking window, and fallback options. Next steps: share SOC2/ISO docs, draft pilot runbook, schedule bench test with 1M token workload next week.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-23 15:00 PST
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Evan (Redwood SE), Liam (Fenwick VP Eng), Renee (Fenwick SecOps), Carlos (Fenwick Platform)
---
Summary: quick intake to align on governance-heavy onboarding. Customer is heavily regulated, wants private VPC deployment and HSM-backed keys, also wants clear rollback and fallbacks.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick intros?
[00:04] Liam: yeah, Liam O'Connor here, VP Eng at Fenwick, we run a mixed SaaS/on-prem product line, we need to understand how Redwood will sit inside our network and meet our security bar.
[00:12] Renee: Renee Park, SecOps, main concerns around key management, audit logs, and least-privilege access.
[00:16] Carlos: Carlos Mendez, platform eng, I'll be doing the bench and the netconfig work.
[00:19] Maya: great, and Evan is our SE who will run the technical bench. Evan?
[00:23] Evan: thanks, hey all — I want to hear constraints first: latency SLOs, data residency, and any hard blockers like no external egress, HSM only for keys, that sort of thing.
[00:32] Liam: so our baseline is we'd like sub-150ms token latency for short prompts (<512 tokens) at the 95th percentile for user-facing features, and for batch jobs we can tolerate higher but want predictable throughput. Cost is important but security is the non-negotiable.
[00:45] Maya: good, that helps. Do you have a preference for deployment mode — hosted api, dedicated reserved pool, or private VPC/on-prem?
[00:52] Liam: we discussed; security team insists on Private VPC with no public model traffic, and KMS via HSM. We still want Redwood ops to help run the pilot but under our network.
[01:05] Evan: got it, private option supports a customer-managed control plane with a gateway inside the VPC. We can integrate with your KMS via standard KMIP or cloud KMS flows, though for HSM there are an extra validation steps.
[01:18] Renee: on the KMS piece, do you have examples of HSM integrations? We run AWS CloudHSM today and have an on-prem Thales HSM for some keys.
[01:27] Evan: yes, we've done both. For CloudHSM we do an HSM proxy pattern inside the VPC and the control plane stores only references; for customer-managed HSMs we can do an out-of-band key-wrap approach. I'll note that that requires an HSM validation workshop and likely additional compliance paperwork.
[01:44] Carlos: firewall wise, what are the minimal egress ports? We have pretty locked down egress policies.
[01:50] Evan: for private, most traffic stays internal. The control plane needs limited egress for updates and telemetry if you allow it; we can opt for disconnected or very limited telemetry. We'll send the exact port list but typical is 443 to specific endpoints, and internal RPC ports between nodes — but those stay in the VPC.
[02:06] Liam: important: audit logs must be immutable and accessible to us for 12 months. Is that something Redwood supports?
[02:13] Maya: yes — our Private offering supports sending audit logs to your S3 or SIEM, and we can also provide hashed immutability proofs. I'll attach the audit log spec.
[02:22] Renee: and retention policies? We have to demonstrate retention and deletion controls for audits.
[02:27] Evan: retention is configurable — on the private deployment you control the storage bucket, lifecycle rules, and encryption. We support per-tenant logging and log-forwarding to Splunk/Datadog.
[02:36] Liam: great. On the performance side, what's your usual approach for benchmarking? We want a realistic bench that covers chat loads and batch embedding generation.
[02:44] Evan: we propose a two-phase bench: first a 1M token synthetic run simulating chat (varied prompt lengths, KV cache warm-up) to measure p50/p95/p99 and token cost; second a batch embedding throughput test with realistic doc sizes. We'll run these in your VPC with your keys.
[03:02] Carlos: what about model variants or fallback for capacity constraints? We can't afford user-facing downtime.
[03:07] Evan: Redwood has routing policies — you can set regional fallback and model-variant fallbacks (quantized or smaller variants) and configurable canary rollouts. For critical endpoints you can pin a dedicated pool. We'll review cost tradeoffs — pinned capacity increases cost but reduces latency variance.
[03:22] Liam: can we do A/B for quality vs cost during pilot?
[03:25] Evan: yes, we can run A/B on responses, collect evals, and feed results into Redwood Optimize recommendations.
[03:32] Renee: compliance checks — do you provide SOC2 and ISO artifacts and an assessor contact?
[03:36] Maya: yes, I'll send the SOC2 + ISO summary and our compliance pack. For private deployments you still get those documents and additional attestations for the private control plane.
[03:46] Liam: timeline — we need a 3-week pilot window before the year-end to validate latency and security. Is that doable?
[03:52] Evan: feasible — we need two weeks for setup (network, KMS, service account permissions), then a one-week bench and tuning window if the network and keys are ready. If Carlos can provide the topology and firewall rules quickly that's the critical path.
[04:07] Carlos: I can get that by Friday, I have to sync with infra and security.
[04:11] Renee: DPA and data residency — we store EU PII in eu-west-1, so any data transfer must stay in-region unless otherwise contracted. Do you support region pinning?
[04:20] Maya: yes, Redwood supports region pinning for private deployments; we'll include data residency clauses in the DPA and our product supports regional model hosting.
[04:29] Liam: we'll also need RBAC mapped to our IdP — SAML or OIDC — and fine grained roles.
[04:35] Evan: both supported; we can sync on the role matrix. We usually map SAML groups to RBAC roles and can provide a sample mapping template.
[04:44] Maya: quick note — cost control: we'll provide batching and caching recommendations, and Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization profiles; however quantization can affect output quality, so we'll include acceptance tests in the pilot.
[04:58] Liam: that's acceptable as long as we have measurable QA checks.
[05:02] Evan: for acceptance criteria, propose: p95 latency <150ms for interactive paths, embedding throughput X docs/sec at Y tokens, and no audit or KMS showstoppers.
[05:12] Maya: ok I'll draft a pilot runbook with those acceptance criteria and send it out.
[05:17] Renee: legal will want to review DPA, encryption-at-rest proofs, and access logs.
[05:21] Maya: noted, legal will reach out; I'll include our DPA template and redwood security FAQ link: https://redwood.example.com/security-packet (link).
[05:29] Carlos: two quick technicals: can we capture request/response traces for debugging, and how is KV cache managed for long chat sessions?
[05:36] Evan: yes traces are supported and can be forwarded to your tracing backend; KV cache is managed per-session and persists on nodes with cache eviction policies. If you have long context needs we recommend prefix caching and larger KV cache configs; we'll share config recommendations.
[05:52] Maya: ok, to recap next steps — I'll send SOC2/ISO pack, DPA template, and pilot runbook; Evan will prepare bench plan and proposed test dates; Carlos to share topology and firewall list; Renee to confirm KMS provider.
[06:05] Liam: thanks, sounds good — let's target the bench for the first week of December.
[06:09] Maya: perfect, we'll send calendar invites with proposed slots.
[06:12] Evan: any questions?
[06:14] Renee: none from me.
[06:15] Liam: no.
[06:16] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the packet and action items.

End transcript.

References mentioned: security packet link (https://redwood.example.com/security-packet), private deployment checklist (will be attached), sample RBAC mapping template (to be shared).
